newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy ends mixed-forecasts weigh on bull spread.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy ends mixed-forecasts weigh on bull spread.

text.p: Forecasts showing the possibility of hot, dry weather in the U.S. Midwest later this week caused losses in July soybeans and rallied new crop months, traders said.
"People looking at forecasts for high heat brought some people out of bull spreads today," said Mark Cermak, a trader for O'Connor and Co in Chicago.
Several U.S. forecasts showed the possibility of a high pressure ridge building up over the Midwest by the end of the week. High pressure ridges typically lock in dry, hot weather.

July also fell as traders exited their positions before first notice day on Monday. Monday is also the day that the U.S. Department of Agriculture issues its latest soybean acreage forecasts and reports quarterly stocks data.

Commodity funds were active buyers in the November contract throughout the session, traders said. Rosenthal Collins bought 10 million bushels of November soybeans, but some traders said the heavy buying was short covering.
In late trading, Refco and Prudential Securities sold one million bushels of July, pit sources said.
CBOT July soybeans ended five cents per bushel down at $8.31 and other months were 8-1/2 higher to 1/2 lower.

Current weather conditions in the U.S. Midwest were considered bearish for futures, traders said. Most areas were receiving hot temperatures ranging from 88 to 94 degrees Fahrenheit, and parts of the western Corn Belt have gotten rain in the last 24 hours.

July also came under pressure from talk that one of the large commercial firms was planning to ship soybeans to Chicago to deliver against the board. No traders could offer confirmation of such a plan, however.
"We hear that rumor everytime the spread loses some ground," said a soybean trader. "I don't think it's true because you can get better prices elsewhere."
In other trade on the day, Cargill sold 1.5 million August, Merrill Lynch sold one million July and three million November. Refco bought five million November, pit traders said.
In options trade, Continental Grain bought 400 August $8.00 calls and sold 400 August $8.75 calls. Smith Barney sold 300 September $7.25 calls.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 61,000 contracts, compared with Monday's actual volume of 56,960 contracts.
